x: Community Playbook Best Practices for Campus DEVCON Events Dear chapter leaders: the community sees DEVCON events as the gold standard. These HQ guidelines turn nationwide retrospectives into operational excellence, so every campus event stays world-class. On this page I. Underpromise and overdeliver II. Creative fundraising and partnerships III. Content strategy and slides IV. Program management V. Speaker and sponsor relations VI. Safety and emergencies VII. Final readiness checklist I. Underpromise and overdeliver Assume risks by default. Plan as if the internet will fail, a speaker will be late, and power will fluctuate. Build strategic buffers of 10–15 minutes so you never cut a speaker’s slot. Commit conservatively. Never promise a partner an attendance number unless you’re sure you can hit 120% of it. Keep a safe space. Follow the HQ Safe Space Guidelines and the Code of Conduct . II. Creative fundraising and partnerships DEVCON is a 17-year-old brand. Use that credibility. Plan 3–6 months ahead. The biggest costs are raffle items, speaker tokens, and organizer meals. Target budget cycles: partner with local DOST, DICT, or school IT organizations during peak cycles like IT Week. Start with a proposal: find official emails of local representatives and send a professional collaboration proposal. Prioritize in-kind sponsorships over cash, due to tax and legal risk. Look for win-win “X-deals”. III. Content strategy and slides Diverse topics: quantum computing, generative AI, web3 and blockchain, robotics, cybersecurity, DevOps, and tech leadership. One master slide file to avoid flash-drive and permission issues. Decks due 3–4 days before, with a calendar reminder to speakers. Collaborate in Canva or Google Slides so the tech team can check content and aspect ratios early. IV. Program management Play the DEVCON loop during registration and breaks (see the Community Playbook ). Arrive 3–4 hours early (4–6 for large summits) for rehearsals and safety checks. Tech-check every speaker : audio, clicker, transitions. Energetic, rehearsed hosts who manage transitions smoothly. V. Speaker and sponsor relations Professional impression: your speaker might be your future employer. Speaker integrity is non-negotiable: never drop a speaker on the day. Shorten breaks or Q&A instead. Logistics 14 days prior: a calendar invite with a map pin, gate number, building, and parking. A dedicated liaison for every guest, from entrance to holding area.
